checks.title: Storage accounts allow public blob access

waf.why: Anonymous reads of blobs are a network and access exposure that the account setting controls.

collector.violations: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.storage/storageaccounts' | where isnull(properties.allowBlobPublicAccess) or properties.allowBlobPublicAccess == true | project id, name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, publicAccess=tostring(properties.allowBlobPublicAccess)

checks.proves: The account-level setting that allows anonymous reads of blobs is on or absent.
checks.doesNotProve: That any container is actually public, or that data is sensitive. An account where the setting is absent (null) is flagged because older accounts allowed anonymous reads when it was absent; whether a given account behaves that way is not read.

checks.title: Storage accounts accept old TLS or plain HTTP

waf.why: The minimum TLS version and the HTTPS-only setting decide whether data in transit is protected by modern encryption.
They also limit what traffic the account accepts.

collector.violations: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.storage/storageaccounts' | where properties.minimumTlsVersion in~ ('TLS1_0','TLS1_1') or properties.supportsHttpsTrafficOnly == false | project id, name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, minTls=tostring(properties.minimumTlsVersion), httpsOnly=tobool(properties.supportsHttpsTrafficOnly)

checks.proves: The minimum TLS version is below 1.2 or secure transfer is off.
checks.doesNotProve: That clients actually use the old protocol, or that data at rest is unencrypted.

checks.title: Network security group allows management ports from the Internet

waf.why: An inbound allow rule from any source on SSH or RDP is traffic that is not isolated or filtered.

collector.violations: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/networksecuritygroups' | mv-expand rule=properties.securityRules | where tostring(rule.properties.access) =~ 'Allow' and tostring(rule.properties.direction) =~ 'Inbound' | where tostring(rule.properties.sourceAddressPrefix) in~ ('*','Internet','0.0.0.0/0') | where tostring(rule.properties.destinationPortRange) in~ ('22','3389','*') | project id, name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, ruleName=tostring(rule.name), port=tostring(rule.properties.destinationPortRange)

checks.proves: A rule of a network security group allows inbound traffic from *, Internet or 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22, 3389 or *.
checks.doesNotProve: Effective reachability after route tables, Azure Firewall or network virtual appliances; rule priority and a deny rule that comes first are not evaluated; rules written with several prefixes or several port ranges (the plural properties) are not inspected. Rows are rules while the evaluated count is network security groups, so the two numbers have different units.

checks.title: SQL servers allow public network access

waf.why: Public network access on a database server is exposure the network layer should filter.

collector.violations: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.sql/servers' | where properties.publicNetworkAccess =~ 'Enabled' | project id, name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, publicNetworkAccess=tostring(properties.publicNetworkAccess)

checks.proves: The public network access setting of the SQL server is Enabled.
checks.doesNotProve: Which firewall rules exist, or whether the server is reachable from the Internet in practice.

checks.title: Key Vaults without purge protection

waf.why: Purge protection keeps deleted secrets and keys recoverable for the retention period.

collector.violations: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.keyvault/vaults' | where properties.enablePurgeProtection != true | project id, name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, purgeProtection=tobool(properties.enablePurgeProtection), softDelete=tobool(properties.enableSoftDelete)

checks.proves: Purge protection of the vault is not enabled.
checks.doesNotProve: Anything about the secrets, keys or access policies; their values are never read.

checks.title: Owner role held by a user at subscription scope

waf.why: A standing Owner assignment to a user is broad, hard to audit access.

collector.evaluated: authorizationresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.authorization/roleassignments' | where tostring(properties.scope) matches regex '^/subscriptions/[^/]+$' | summarize n=count()
collector.violations: authorizationresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.authorization/roleassignments' | where tostring(properties.scope) matches regex '^/subscriptions/[^/]+$' | where tostring(properties.roleDefinitionId) endswith '/8e3af657-a8ff-443c-a75c-2fe8c4bcb635' and tostring(properties.principalType) =~ 'User' | extend principalId=tostring(properties.principalId), principalType=tostring(properties.principalType), roleName='Owner', scope=tostring(properties.scope) | project id, subscriptionId, principalId, principalType, roleName, scope

checks.proves: A role assignment of Owner at subscription scope has a principal of type User.
checks.doesNotProve: Who the principal is (that needs Microsoft Graph), whether the assignment is eligible or active in PIM, or assignments at other scopes.

checks.title: Defender for Cloud plans are off

waf.why: Defender plans are threat detection mechanisms integrated with the platform.
Their coverage is part of the baseline that is measured.

collector.violations: securityresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.security/pricings' | where tostring(properties.pricingTier) =~ 'Free' | project id, name, subscriptionId, tier=tostring(properties.pricingTier)

text.en: Which Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans are enabled on the production subscriptions, and who reviews its recommendations?
text.pt-BR: Quais planos do Microsoft Defender for Cloud estão habilitados nas assinaturas de produção, e quem revisa as recomendações?

checks.proves: The pricing tier of a Defender for Cloud plan is Free.
checks.doesNotProve: Whether another product covers the same resources, or whether alerts are acted on.

checks.title: Defender assessments unhealthy

waf.why: Unhealthy assessments show where the baseline is not met.

collector.violations: securityresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.security/assessments' | where tostring(properties.status.code) =~ 'Unhealthy' | project id, subscriptionId, displayName=tostring(properties.displayName), severity=tostring(properties.metadata.severity)

checks.proves: Defender for Cloud reports the assessment as Unhealthy for the resource.
checks.doesNotProve: That the finding is exploitable, or that the assessment list is complete (assessments for plans that are off do not exist).

checks.title: Subscription with no policy assignment

waf.why: A policy baseline is how a security baseline is applied at scale.

collector.violations: resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions' | join kind=leftouter (policyresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.authorization/policyassignments' | extend subIdR=subscriptionId | project subIdR) on $left.subscriptionId == $right.subIdR | where isnull(subIdR) | project id, name, subscriptionId

checks.proves: No Azure Policy assignment is recorded for the subscription.
checks.doesNotProve: Assignments at management group scope that apply to it (the check looks at subscription-level records only), or the quality of the policies.

checks.title: Identity controls in Microsoft Entra ID

waf.why: Conditional Access, MFA and privileged access are identity practices Azure RBAC data does not show.

text.en: Is multi-factor authentication enforced for all administrators, and is privileged access time-limited (for example PIM)?
text.pt-BR: A autenticação multifator é exigida de todos os administradores, e o acesso privilegiado tem prazo (por exemplo, PIM)?

checks.proves: The answer of the person who knows the practice.
checks.doesNotProve: The actual configuration; Microsoft Entra ID is not read in v1.
